links.note: Why diffusion cannot meet the oxygen need of a large multicellular body - the textbook's opening argument for why life processes need specialised systems (151), not the structure of the human respiratory system (161), which the item never asks about.
Criteria for deciding something is alive (movement, growth, molecular maintenance) - the definition of life processes (151).

Outside raw materials an organism uses (food, CO2, minerals, water, oxygen) - the material-exchange half of the life-processes definition (151), spanning both nutrition modes rather than sitting in 152 or 155.
Role of stomach HCl is defined by what it does for the enzyme: activates pepsinogen and supplies pepsin's acid medium (157). 156 would be the organ tour; this item is about enzymatic action.
Villi, microvilli and capillary supply of the small intestine - gross design of the alimentary canal for absorption (156), not enzyme action (157).
Urine volume regulated by blood volume and ADH acting on the nephron tubule (168).
Alveolar design and the 80 m2 of respiratory surface - a structure fact of the human respiratory system (161), not the biochemical respiration pathway (159).
Haemoglobin deficiency and its effect on oxygen carriage - blood as the transport medium (162). 165 is the vessels, 163 the pump; neither carries the oxygen.
Xylem versus phloem transport, contents, direction and driving force - the plant vascular transport concept (166). 167 is only the pull that moves xylem sap.
Functions of the leaf epidermis, given as protection plus bearing the stomata for gas exchange and transpiration - the stomata concept (154) is the only one covering the epidermis.
Diagram identified as double circulation with pulmonary (A) and systemic (B) circuits (164), not general circulatory anatomy (162).
A girdled tree dies because removing the bark removes phloem and starves the roots - phloem translocation (166). 167 concerns xylem and would not be affected by girdling.
Why multicellular organisms need special gas-exchange organs: most cells are not in contact with the environment - the life-processes argument (151), not respiratory anatomy (161).

Autotroph versus heterotroph compared on food source, chlorophyll and energy. Filed on 152 because the discriminating property being tested is self-synthesis of food; 155 is the same axis seen from the other side.
Vaseline on leaves blocks the stomata, so gas exchange and transpiration stop (154). Not 153 - photosynthesis fails only as a consequence of the blocked pore.
Artery versus vein on direction, pressure, wall thickness and valves - the blood-vessel types concept (165).
Why a herbivore's small intestine is longer - length of the alimentary canal set by diet and cellulose digestion time (156).
Without mucus the stomach lining is corroded into an ulcer - a protective feature of the stomach wall (156). Mucus is not an enzyme, so not 157.
Emulsification matters because fine fat globules let lipase act efficiently - the item is about enzyme action on substrate (157), not about the organ (156).
What moves food along the gut - peristalsis by name (158).
Absorption happens mainly in the small intestine because digestion completes there and villi/microvilli give the surface - alimentary-canal design (156).
Cuscuta, ticks and leeches are all parasites - the parasitic branch of heterotrophic nutrition (155), not saprophytic or holozoic.
Functions of gastric-gland secretions, answered as pepsin, rennin, gastric lipase plus HCl and mucus - the item is carried by the digestive enzymes (157).
Matches trypsin/amylase/bile/pepsin to their sources - enzyme-and-secretion identification (157).
Veins have thin walls because blood is not under pressure, and carry valves instead - a property of vessel types (165).

Water enters root xylem continuously because active ion uptake raises osmotic concentration there - root-to-xylem water entry (166). 167 is the transpiration pull higher up the column, which this item does not invoke.
Describe the human alimentary canal end to end - 156 exactly.
What we take from and return to the environment - the material-exchange requirement of life processes (151). The closing environmental-values clause matches no concept here.
Names xylem as the water and mineral conducting tissue (166).
How autotrophs obtain CO2 from air and nitrogen as nitrate/ammonium from soil - raw materials of autotrophic nutrition (152). 153 is the light reaction chemistry, not the sourcing.
Names trypsin as the protein-digesting pancreatic enzyme (157).
Names salivary amylase/ptyalin as the starch-splitting enzyme (157).
Role of stomach acid, answered as disinfection plus acidifying for pepsin - enzyme-linked (157). Duplicate stem of qid:85600.
Bread mould and mushroom feed saprophytically by secreting enzymes onto external organic matter - the saprophytic branch of heterotrophic nutrition (155).
Starch is not digested in the stomach because gastric juice carries no amylase - the answer is an enzyme-distribution fact (157).
Purpose of making urine: extracting soluble wastes from blood for expulsion (168).
Ventricles have thicker walls than atria because of the distance they pump against - heart chamber structure and function (163), not the vessels (165).
The air passage stays open on expiration because of cartilage rings - an air-passage structure fact of the respiratory system (161).
Organisms that use CO2 and water as food are autotrophs (152).
Why the trachea carries cartilage rings - respiratory passage structure (161). Duplicate demand of qid:85718.
Defines excretion and asks how unicellular organisms void wastes. Filed on 168, the chapter's only excretion concept; the unicellular-diffusion half has no concept of its own.
What the amount of water reabsorbed by the nephron tubule depends on (168).
Two differences between arteries and veins (165).
Vaseline-coated leaves of a potted plant - blocked stomata stop gas exchange and transpiration (154). Duplicate stem of qid:85649.
